First, we express

$$
f(x)=5(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{8}.
$$

Now, we see that $f(x)$ can be expressed as the composite function

$$
f=5{u}^{8},\,u=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=40{u}^{7},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =40{u}^{7}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =40(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{7}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =-40{cos}^{7}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
